segments.text: Morning, everyone. Thanks for making the time. Before we start, I'd like to confirm what we agreed by email. I'm using the meeting's transcript to write up the requirements, and the AI that helps me runs on my own computer. Is that still fine with both of you?
Yes, that's fine with me.
Ja, fine.
Thank you. So the goal today is to understand how dispatch works now and what the app has to do. Thandi, do you want to start with the problem?

Sure. We run forty trucks between Gauteng and the Western Cape, out of two depots, Midrand and Bloemfontein. Dispatch happens on WhatsApp. The controller posts the collections in a group, the drivers reply, and then somebody types it all into a shared spreadsheet at night. We miss collections because messages get buried.
How many collections is that on a normal day?
About a hundred and twenty a day. In November and December it roughly doubles.
On the bad days in December we've had two hundred and sixty.
And what does a missed collection cost you?
A re-delivery is about eighteen hundred rand, and we lose the client's trust, which is worse. Last December we lost one retail account over it.
So the app has to make sure every collection is assigned and confirmed. What does a driver need to do on the road?

Accept the job, mark it collected, take a photo of the waybill, and get a signature. But you must understand, between Colesberg and Beaufort West there's no signal for hours. It has to work offline and send everything when they're back in range.
That's an important constraint. Do the drivers all have smartphones?
Most have Android phones, their own. I think they all do, but I'd have to check. A few of the older guys still use basic phones.
We'd rather not buy phones for everyone if we can avoid it.
Understood. Which systems would this have to work with?

Our trucks have a tracking system from a vendor, so we can see where they are. And invoicing runs on Sage. It would be nice if the app could pull positions from the tracking system, but it's not essential at the start.
Who decides on the budget for this?
Our MD signs off anything above two hundred thousand rand. I'd want to show her a figure by the end of January.
Sorry I'm late, I was stuck in another call. I look after their network and the depot computers.
Welcome, Lerato. We were just talking about offline use. How reliable is the internet at the depots?
Midrand is fine. Bloemfontein goes down during load-shedding because the router isn't on the backup battery. That should be fixed, but it isn't yet.
And when it's down, the controller can't see anything.
Then the controller's screen needs to cope with the depot being offline too. One more thing. Drivers' locations are personal information. Have you checked how you're allowed to use them?
Not yet. HR would have to look at that with the drivers' union.
I'll note it as an open question. Last thing: is there anything you'd want later, but not in the first version?
Eventually our clients should get a tracking link, like a courier. But not now.
And Afrikaans in the app. Half my drivers would prefer it.
Good. My suggestion is to start with a pilot at the Bloemfontein depot, since it has the hardest conditions. Does that work?
Yes, let's do Bloemfontein first.
Great. I'll send a summary this afternoon. Thank you, everyone.
